schlacht-auf-dem-kulikowo-feld#summary: Grand Prince Dmitry of Moscow defeats the army of the warlord Mamai on the Don; it is the first great victory of the Rus over the Golden Horde.
schlacht-auf-dem-kulikowo-feld#text: From 1359 rival khans and warlords fought for power within the Golden Horde. The warlord Mamai wanted to force the princes of Moscow to pay tribute again and allied himself with Lithuania. On 8 September 1380 Dmitry, who received the byname Donskoy after the place on the Don, met him on the field of Kulikovo with forces from several principalities and defeated him at heavy cost. Two years later Khan Tokhtamysh burned Moscow, and tribute payments continued. Nevertheless, in chronicles and legends the victory became a sign that the Horde could be beaten and that Moscow could claim leadership of the Rus.
union-von-krewo#summary: Grand Duke Jogaila of Lithuania pledges to become a Christian and to marry Queen Jadwiga of Poland; Poland and Lithuania are joined in a personal union.
union-von-krewo#text: In the 14th century Lithuania was the last pagan great power in Europe and had conquered large parts of the former Rus as far as the Dnieper, including much of present-day Ukraine and Belarus. Under pressure from the Teutonic Order, Grand Duke Jogaila concluded a treaty with the Polish nobility at Krewo on 14 August 1385. In 1386 he was baptized with the name Władysław, married the young Queen Jadwiga and was crowned king of Poland; in 1387 the baptism of the Lithuanians began. Under Jogaila's cousin Vytautas, Lithuania kept extensive autonomy. The Jagiellonian dynasty ruled until 1572 and at times also governed Bohemia and Hungary.
kalmarer-union#summary: At Kalmar, Eric of Pomerania is crowned king of Denmark, Norway and Sweden; Margaret I thus unites all Scandinavia under one crown.
kalmarer-union#text: Margaret, daughter of Valdemar IV and widow of the Norwegian king Haakon VI, ruled Denmark and Norway after the death of her son Olaf in 1387 and, with her victory over Albert of Mecklenburg in 1389, also won Sweden. In June 1397 she had her great-nephew Eric of Pomerania crowned joint king at Kalmar; a union charter drafted there, whose legal force is disputed, provided that the realms should have one king but be governed according to their own laws. Real power was exercised by Margaret until her death in 1412. The union suffered from the resistance of the Swedish nobility and finally broke apart in 1523.
schlacht-bei-grunwald#summary: A Polish-Lithuanian army defeats the army of the Teutonic Order; the grand master falls, and the Order's power begins to wane.
schlacht-bei-grunwald#text: The conflict over Samogitia and the Baltic coast led in 1409 to war between the Teutonic Order and Poland-Lithuania. On 15 July 1410 the armies met between the villages of Grunwald and Tannenberg in what is now northern Poland. King Władysław II Jagiełło and Grand Duke Vytautas, supported by Ruthenian, Tatar and Bohemian warriors, won a complete victory; Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen fell along with many knights of the Order. The victors could not take Marienburg, and the First Peace of Thorn in 1411 brought only small territorial gains. For Poland and Lithuania, where it is called Žalgiris, the battle became a central place of national memory.
konzil-von-konstanz#summary: A church council on Lake Constance ends the Great Western Schism and condemns the Prague reformer Jan Hus to death.
konzil-von-konstanz#text: Since 1378 two popes, and from 1409 even three, had contended for leadership of the Church. At the urging of King Sigismund a council met at Constance in 1414 and declared itself superior to the pope. It deposed the popes or accepted their resignation and in 1417 elected Martin V, which ended the schism. At the same time the council had Jan Hus burned as a heretic in 1415 despite the safe conduct promised to him, and a year later his ally Jerome of Prague as well. The execution sparked the Hussite Wars in Bohemia.
union-von-florenz#summary: Hoping for Western help against the Ottomans, the emperor and church representatives sign a union with Rome.
union-von-florenz#text: Emperor John VIII Palaiologos travelled with the patriarch and numerous bishops to the Council of Ferrara and Florence. On 6 July 1439 the union was proclaimed, in which the Greek participants accepted papal primacy and the Filioque. In Byzantium large parts of the clergy and the population firmly rejected the union, and the hoped-for help largely failed to arrive: a crusade was defeated at Varna in 1444. Some participants, such as Bessarion, remained in Italy and promoted the study of Greek there.
moskau-unterwirft-nowgorod#summary: Ivan III ends the independence of the city republic of Novgorod and has its veche bell taken to Moscow.
moskau-unterwirft-nowgorod#text: Novgorod controlled a vast territory reaching to the White Sea and the Urals and was governed by a popular assembly, the veche, and an upper class of wealthy boyars. When one party in the city sought support from Lithuania, Ivan III marched against Novgorod in 1471 and defeated its army on the river Shelon. In 1478 the city had to submit for good; the bell that had summoned the veche was taken to Moscow, and many boyar families were resettled. In 1494 Ivan also had the Hanseatic trading post closed. With Novgorod, Moscow gained access to the fur lands of the north.
stehen-an-der-ugra#title: The Great Stand on the Ugra
stehen-an-der-ugra#summary: The armies of Moscow and the Great Horde face each other for weeks on the Ugra until the khan withdraws; Tatar rule over Moscow is over.
stehen-an-der-ugra#text: Ivan III had stopped paying tribute to the Horde. In the autumn of 1480 Khan Akhmat of the Great Horde, a successor state of the Golden Horde, advanced with an army and hoped for help from Lithuania, which never came. On the Ugra, a tributary of the Oka, the two armies faced each other for weeks without a major battle. When the frost set in, Akhmat withdrew; he was murdered the following year. Later historians set 1480 as the end of the "Tatar yoke"; the term is disputed because dependence had already loosened before then. From now on Moscow paid no more tribute and acted as an independent great power.
portugiesen-erobern-malakka#summary: Afonso de Albuquerque captures the most important trading port in Southeast Asia and opens the European colonial era in the region.
portugiesen-erobern-malakka#text: In August 1511 Afonso de Albuquerque attacked Malacca with a fleet from Goa and took the city after fierce fighting; Sultan Mahmud Shah fled, and his descendants founded the Sultanate of Johor. The Portuguese built the fortress of A Famosa and aimed to control the spice trade; their ships reached the Moluccas as early as 1512. They never achieved their goal of dominating trade, however: Muslim merchants moved to Aceh, Johor and the north coast of Java, which now flourished. In Malacca the apothecary Tomé Pires described Asia's trading network in his Suma Oriental. In 1641 the Dutch East India Company, together with Johor, captured the city.
magellan-erreicht-guam#title: Magellan crosses the Pacific and reaches Guam
magellan-erreicht-guam#summary: After more than three months on the open ocean, the Spanish fleet under Ferdinand Magellan reaches the Marianas – the first known crossing of the Pacific by Europeans.
magellan-erreicht-guam#text: In November 1520 Magellan left the strait at the southern tip of America that bears his name and called the calm sea the "Pacific". The crossing took far longer than expected, and many sailors died of scurvy and hunger. On 6 March 1521 the ships reached Guam, where barter with the Chamorro soon turned to violence; the Spaniards named the island group the "Islands of Thieves". Magellan was killed a few weeks later in the Philippines, and Juan Sebastián Elcano completed the circumnavigation in 1522. Spain colonized the Marianas from 1668.
iwan-iv-wird-zar#summary: The sixteen-year-old Grand Prince Ivan is solemnly crowned tsar in Moscow, the first Russian ruler to be so.
iwan-iv-wird-zar#text: Ivan had become grand prince in 1533 at the age of three; during his childhood boyar families struggled for power. On 16 January 1547 Metropolitan Makary crowned him tsar in the Cathedral of the Dormition in the Kremlin. The title, derived from the Latin "Caesar", put the ruler of Moscow on a level with the Byzantine emperor and the khan of the Horde. In the first years of his reign Ivan convened an assembly of the land, had a new law code drawn up in 1550 and created a force armed with firearms, the streltsy. From 1721 the official title was emperor, but "tsar" remained the common designation of Russia's rulers until 1917.
eroberung-von-kasan#summary: Ivan IV conquers the Khanate of Kazan on the Volga; four years later Astrakhan also falls, and Russia becomes a multi-ethnic empire.
eroberung-von-kasan#text: The Khanate of Kazan was one of the successor states of the Golden Horde and repeatedly raided Muscovite territory. After several failed campaigns, Ivan IV had the city besieged by a large army in 1552; sappers blew up the walls, and on 2 October Kazan was stormed and many of its inhabitants were killed. The Khanate of Astrakhan at the mouth of the Volga followed in 1556. Moscow now controlled the entire course of the Volga, and Tatars, Chuvash, Mari and Bashkirs became subjects of the tsar. St Basil's Cathedral on Red Square was built to commemorate the victory.
opritschnina#summary: Ivan IV divides the realm and has his bodyguard, the oprichniki, terrorize nobles, clergy and entire towns.
opritschnina#text: After defeats in the Livonian War and the death of his first wife, Ivan IV grew increasingly distrustful of the boyars. At the beginning of 1565 he declared part of the country his personal domain, the oprichnina, and raised a black-clad force to hunt down traitors. The oprichniki expropriated and murdered numerous boyars and their peasants; Metropolitan Philip, who had publicly criticized Ivan, was strangled in 1569. At the beginning of 1570 they laid waste to Novgorod and killed thousands of its inhabitants; exact figures are not known. After the Crimean Tatars burned Moscow in 1571, Ivan dissolved the oprichnina in 1572. The country was left devastated and depopulated.
union-von-lublin#summary: Poland and Lithuania merge into the Commonwealth of the Two Nations with a common king and parliament.
union-von-lublin#text: Since 1385 Poland and Lithuania had been linked only through their rulers. Threatened by Moscow in the Livonian War, the Lithuanian nobility agreed to a closer union at the Sejm in Lublin on 1 July 1569, after the king had transferred the Ukrainian lands of Volhynia, Bracław and Kyiv as well as Podlachia from Lithuania to the Polish Crown. The new Rzeczpospolita had a common king, elected by the nobility from 1573, a common Sejm and a common foreign policy; Lithuania kept its own offices, laws, army and treasury. At times covering almost a million square kilometres, it was one of the largest states in Europe. The Warsaw Confederation of 1573 also guaranteed the nobility an unusually far-reaching freedom of religion.
spanier-gruenden-manila#summary: Miguel López de Legazpi makes Manila the capital of the Spanish colony in the Philippines, which will last for more than 300 years.
spanier-gruenden-manila#text: Magellan had reached the islands in 1521 and was killed on Mactan fighting the warriors of Lapulapu. In 1543 a further expedition named them "Las Islas Filipinas" after the heir to the throne, Philip. In 1565 Legazpi landed on Cebu, and in the same year his companion Andrés de Urdaneta found the return route to Mexico. In 1571 Legazpi captured the settlement of Maynila, ruled by the chief Sulayman, on Manila Bay and founded the Spanish capital there. Until 1815 the galleon sailed from Manila to Acapulco, carrying Chinese silk and porcelain in exchange for American silver. Friars made Catholicism the majority religion, while the sultanates of Sulu and Mindanao long resisted Spanish rule.
zeit-der-wirren#summary: After the Muscovite Rurikids die out, famine, false pretenders, uprisings and foreign armies plunge the Muscovite state into a deep crisis.
zeit-der-wirren#text: With the death of the childless Tsar Fyodor I in 1598 the Muscovite line of the Rurikids died out. His brother-in-law Boris Godunov was elected tsar, but a famine from 1601 to 1603 cost hundreds of thousands of lives. A man claiming to be Fyodor's dead brother Dmitry entered Moscow with Polish support in 1605 and was murdered a year later; further false Dmitrys and peasant uprisings followed. In 1610 Polish-Lithuanian troops occupied Moscow, and in 1611 Sweden took Novgorod. Only a popular militia under the merchant Kuzma Minin and Prince Dmitry Pozharsky drove the occupiers out of the Kremlin in 1612.
wahl-michail-romanows#summary: An assembly of the land elects the sixteen-year-old Michael Romanov tsar; his family rules Russia for more than three centuries.
wahl-michail-romanows#text: After the liberation of Moscow the Zemsky Sobor met at the beginning of 1613, an assembly of representatives of the nobility, the clergy, the towns and the Cossacks. In February it elected the young Michael Romanov, whose family was related by marriage to the extinct dynasty. His father Filaret, who returned from Polish captivity and became patriarch, was effectively co-ruler until 1633. The peace treaties with Sweden in 1617 and Poland-Lithuania in 1618 cost territory but ended the Troubles. The Romanovs ruled until the abdication of Nicholas II in March 1917.
voc-gruendet-batavia#title: The Dutch East India Company Founds Batavia
voc-gruendet-batavia#summary: Jan Pieterszoon Coen destroys Jayakarta on Java and founds Batavia in its place, the centre of Dutch power in Asia.
voc-gruendet-batavia#text: The United East India Company, or VOC, founded in 1602, held the Dutch monopoly on trade with Asia and was allowed to build forts, wage war and conclude treaties. In 1619 its governor-general Jan Pieterszoon Coen captured the port city of Jayakarta and founded Batavia, today's Jakarta, on the site. To enforce the monopoly on nutmeg, Coen had the Banda Islands conquered in 1621; a large part of the population was killed, enslaved or driven out. The VOC pushed out the Portuguese and English, took Malacca in 1641 and Makassar in 1667, and extended its rule over Java. At the end of 1799 the heavily indebted company was dissolved and its possessions passed to the Dutch state.
tasmans-reise#title: Abel Tasman reaches Tasmania and New Zealand
tasmans-reise#summary: Sailing for the Dutch East India Company, Abel Tasman becomes the first known European to sight Tasmania and New Zealand.
tasmans-reise#text: In 1642 the Dutch East India Company sent Tasman out from Batavia to explore the supposed Southern Land. On 24 November he sighted the coast of an island that he named Van Diemen's Land after the governor-general – today's Tasmania. In December he reached the South Island of New Zealand; in a bay at the northern end of the South Island, Māori attacked a ship's boat and killed four sailors, whereupon Tasman sailed on without going ashore. On the return voyage in early 1643 he visited Tonga and Fiji. The Company regarded the voyage as unprofitable because it yielded no trade goods.
chmelnyzkyj-aufstand#summary: The Zaporozhian Cossacks rise against Poland-Lithuania under Bohdan Khmelnytsky and found a Hetmanate of their own in Ukraine.
chmelnyzkyj-aufstand#text: In Ukraine, Cossacks, Orthodox peasants and clergy felt oppressed by the Polish nobility and their estate managers. In the spring of 1648 the Cossack officer Bohdan Khmelnytsky, allied with the Crimean Tatars, led an uprising that defeated the Polish armies at Zhovti Vody and Korsun and grew into a people's war. In the fighting tens of thousands of Jews, Poles and Catholics were murdered; the exact numbers are disputed, and the events still shape Jewish memory today. Khmelnytsky established a Hetmanate and in January 1654 at Pereiaslav placed himself under the tsar, which triggered a war between Moscow and Poland-Lithuania. Whether Pereiaslav was an alliance or a submission is still interpreted differently by Ukrainian and Russian historians. In 1667 Ukraine was divided between the two powers along the Dnieper.
kirchenspaltung-raskol#summary: A council in Moscow confirms the reforms of Patriarch Nikon; their opponents, the Old Believers, are excluded from the church and persecuted.
kirchenspaltung-raskol#text: From 1653 Patriarch Nikon had the service books and rites of the Russian church brought into line with Greek models; among other things, believers were to cross themselves with three fingers instead of two. Many priests and believers saw this as a betrayal of the inherited faith. The council of 1666 and 1667 deposed Nikon because of his power struggle with the tsar but confirmed his reforms and condemned their opponents. Archpriest Avvakum, their best-known spokesman, was burned in 1682, and the Solovetsky Monastery put up armed resistance for years. The Old Believers survive as separate communities to this day.
schlacht-bei-poltawa#summary: In present-day Ukraine, Peter the Great defeats the army of Charles XII; Sweden's age as a great power comes to an end, and Russia becomes the leading power in Eastern Europe.
schlacht-bei-poltawa#text: In the Great Northern War, Charles XII of Sweden, after victories over Denmark, Poland-Lithuania and Russia, advanced into Ukraine in 1708, where the Cossack hetman Ivan Mazepa joined him. Russian troops then destroyed Mazepa's residence at Baturyn and killed many of its inhabitants. On 8 July 1709 Peter's numerically superior, newly organized army crushed the weakened Swedes at Poltava. Charles XII and Mazepa fled to the Ottoman Empire. In the Treaty of Nystad in 1721 Russia received Livonia, Estonia and Ingria with the new St Petersburg, and Peter took the title of emperor. The autonomy of the Hetmanate was dismantled step by step in the following decades.
makassarischer-trepanghandel#title: Macassan trepang fishers in northern Australia
makassarischer-trepanghandel#summary: Seafarers from Makassar on Sulawesi visit the coast of Arnhem Land every year to gather sea cucumbers and trade with the Yolŋu.
makassarischer-trepanghandel#text: From around the early 18th century, possibly earlier, fleets from Makassar sailed with the northwest monsoon to the northern coast of Australia, which they called "Marege". There they gathered, boiled and dried trepang – sea cucumbers that were sold to China as a delicacy and medicine. They traded cloth, metal tools, tobacco and rice with the Yolŋu and other Aboriginal people, and some Aboriginal people sailed with them to Sulawesi. Macassan words entered the languages of Arnhem Land, and the encounters found their way into rock art, songs and ceremonies. From 1906 the government of South Australia, which administered the Northern Territory, refused the necessary licences, and the last fleet came in 1907.
fall-von-ayutthaya#summary: Troops of the Burmese Konbaung dynasty capture and destroy Ayutthaya, capital of Siam for more than 400 years.
fall-von-ayutthaya#text: Ayutthaya had been the capital of Siam since 1351 and in the 17th century was one of Asia's great trading cities. In Burma Alaungpaya had founded the Konbaung dynasty in 1752 and reunited the country; he died in 1760 during a campaign against Siam. His son Hsinbyushin had Ayutthaya besieged from 1765; in April 1767 the city fell and was burned, and thousands of people were deported to Burma. The general Taksin gathered troops, drove out the Burmese and ruled from Thonburi. In 1782 Rama I founded the Chakri dynasty and made Bangkok, on the opposite bank, the capital, which it remains today.
teilungen-polens#summary: Russia, Prussia and Austria divide the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth among themselves in three steps until it disappears from the map in 1795.
teilungen-polens#text: In the 18th century the nobles' republic was weakened by the liberum veto, civil wars and foreign interference; Russia in effect decided the election of the king. In 1772 Russia, Prussia and Austria annexed almost a third of its territory. When the state reformed itself with the Constitution of 3 May 1791, conservative magnates at Targowica called on Russia for help, and in 1793 Russia and Prussia carried out a second partition. After the suppression of the uprising under Tadeusz Kościuszko in 1794, the three powers divided the remainder in 1795. Russia received the largest share, with Lithuania, Belarus and Ukraine west of the Dnieper except Galicia, which went to Austria. Poland did not become an independent state again until 1918, and the same was true of Lithuania.
pugatschow-aufstand#summary: The Don Cossack Yemelyan Pugachev claims to be Tsar Peter III and leads Cossacks, serfs and steppe peoples in the largest peasant uprising of the tsarist empire.
pugatschow-aufstand#text: Pugachev claimed to be Tsar Peter III, who had been overthrown and murdered in 1762, and promised Cossacks, serfs, Urals workers and Bashkirs freedom from landlords and taxes. From September 1773 his followers captured fortresses on the Yaik and the Volga, killed hundreds of nobles and took Kazan in 1774. Only after peace with the Ottomans could Catherine the Great send enough troops; Pugachev was betrayed and executed in Moscow in January 1775. The empress had the river Yaik renamed the Ural, reorganized provincial administration and afterwards relied even more heavily on the nobility.
ankunft-der-first-fleet#summary: Eleven British ships carrying convicts, soldiers and officials reach Australia; the penal colony of New South Wales is established at Sydney Cove.
ankunft-der-first-fleet#text: After losing its American colonies, Britain looked for a new destination for transported convicts and followed Cook's report on Botany Bay. In January 1788 eleven ships under Governor Arthur Phillip, carrying some 1,400 people including about 750 convicts, reached the bay. Because it seemed unsuitable, the fleet moved on to Port Jackson, where on 26 January Phillip had the British flag raised at Sydney Cove. The land of the Eora was taken without a treaty, as though it belonged to no one. Today 26 January is the national day, but many Aboriginal people regard it as "Invasion Day".
pockenepidemie-in-sydney#title: Smallpox epidemic among Aboriginal people around Sydney
pockenepidemie-in-sydney#summary: A smallpox epidemic kills a large part of the Eora and neighbouring groups.
pockenepidemie-in-sydney#text: In April 1789, just over a year after the British arrived, settlers found many dead and sick people along the shores of Port Jackson. The disease, usually identified as smallpox, spread rapidly among Aboriginal people while the colonists were hardly affected; according to contemporary estimates about half of the population in the surrounding area died. Arabanoo, an Eora man held captive by the British, also succumbed to the disease in May 1789. Where the pathogen came from – the fleet's supplies, Macassan seafarers in the north or some other route – is still disputed. The epidemic severely weakened the communities and eased the further expansion of the colony.
verfassung-vom-3-mai-1791#summary: The Polish-Lithuanian parliament adopts a constitution that abolishes the liberum veto and fundamentally reforms the state.
verfassung-vom-3-mai-1791#text: After the first partition, reformers around King Stanisław August Poniatowski tried to renew the Commonwealth. On 3 May 1791 the Four-Year Sejm adopted a constitution that is regarded, after that of the United States, as the first modern written constitution in Europe. It abolished the liberum veto, introduced hereditary monarchy and a separation of powers, gave townspeople more rights and placed the peasants under the protection of the law. Russia saw it as a threat to its influence and invaded in 1792. The 3rd of May is still a Polish national holiday.
kamehameha-vereinigt-hawaii#title: Kamehameha I unifies the Hawaiian Islands
kamehameha-vereinigt-hawaii#summary: With European weapons and advisers, Kamehameha subdues his rival rulers and creates the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi.
kamehameha-vereinigt-hawaii#text: After Cook's visit in 1778/79 more and more trading ships came to Hawaiʻi, and the chiefs acquired muskets and cannon. Kamehameha, a chief from the island of Hawaiʻi, prevailed in long wars and in 1795 conquered Maui, Molokaʻi and Oʻahu; at the Battle of Nuʻuanu he drove the warriors of Oʻahu to the cliffs of the Pali. In 1810 Kaumualiʻi, the ruler of Kauaʻi and Niʻihau, also submitted without a fight. The unified Kingdom of Hawaiʻi lasted until 1893.
missionare-auf-tahiti#title: The first Protestant missionaries reach Tahiti
missionare-auf-tahiti#summary: Missionaries of the London Missionary Society land on Tahiti from the ship Duff and begin the Christianization of Polynesia.
missionare-auf-tahiti#text: The London Missionary Society, founded in 1795, sent the ship Duff with missionaries and artisans into the Pacific; in March 1797 most of them landed on Tahiti, while the ship put others ashore on Tonga and the Marquesas. At first there were no conversions, and many missionaries left the islands again. Only when Pōmare II, who consolidated his rule with their support, professed Christianity and defeated his opponents in 1815 did many Tahitians follow him. From Tahiti, Polynesian teachers and European missionaries carried Christianity to the Cook Islands, Samoa and further west; in the 19th century almost all the Pacific islands became Christian.
gia-long-eint-vietnam#summary: After defeating the Tây Sơn, Nguyễn Ánh founds the Nguyễn dynasty as Emperor Gia Long and becomes the first to rule all of Vietnam, from Huế.
gia-long-eint-vietnam#text: In the 17th and 18th centuries Đại Việt was divided between the Trịnh lords in the north and the Nguyễn lords in the south. The Tây Sơn brothers' rebellion from 1771 overthrew both houses. The Nguyễn prince Nguyễn Ánh survived and, with help from Siam, French volunteers and Bishop Pigneau de Behaine, regained the south and took Thăng Long in 1802. As Emperor Gia Long he made Huế his capital, built a citadel there and in 1804 obtained China's recognition of the country's name, Việt Nam. His law code followed the Qing model. The Nguyễn dynasty formally lasted until 1945, but from the 1880s it was under French control.
musketenkriege#title: The Musket Wars in New Zealand
musketenkriege#summary: Armed with firearms traded from Europeans, Māori tribes wage wars against one another for decades that claim thousands of lives.
musketenkriege#text: From the end of the 18th century Māori traded flax, pigs, potatoes and timber with whalers and merchants for muskets. Tribes with early access to guns, above all the Ngāpuhi in the north under Hongi Hika, launched long-range campaigns to the south from about 1818, and other groups armed themselves in turn. Fighting, famine and migrations changed the territories of many tribes. How many people died is uncertain; estimates usually put the figure at around 20,000. Once most tribes were armed and Christianity gained influence, the wars subsided in the 1830s.
aufhebung-des-kapu#summary: Shortly after the death of Kamehameha I, the new king and the regent Kaʻahumanu publicly break the religious prohibitions and overturn the old order.
aufhebung-des-kapu#text: The kapu system determined what was sacred and forbidden in Hawaiʻi; among other things, men and women were not allowed to eat together, and violations could be punished by death. After Kamehameha's death in May 1819, Kaʻahumanu, the most influential of his wives, together with the queen mother Keōpūolani, persuaded the new king Liholiho (Kamehameha II) to eat with women at a feast. He then had temples destroyed and images of the gods burned; an uprising by supporters of the old religion was crushed at the end of 1819. When the first American missionaries arrived in 1820, they found a society without its old state cult.
raffles-gruendet-singapur#summary: Stamford Raffles acquires the island of Singapore for the British East India Company and makes it a free port on the Strait of Malacca.
